o1.biggest_strength: It opens with the in-app checkout bug, sized correctly (1,860 more checkouts, about 558 orders, ₹34 lakh a month) and fixed before any test. Sample sizes are honest and right: 9.9% on orders per session, 6.3% on mobile add to cart, each with a rupee value.
o1.biggest_mistake: Test 5 (hero image) rests on thin evidence and takes a slot that a firmness test could have used. The text is also dense, with jargon like "server-side split" and "named segment", and it runs over 1,500 words.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Plainer language, a firmness-in-plain-words test in place of the hero image, and a trimmed word count.

o2.biggest_strength: The funnel table by device and browser makes the in-app bug obvious. It matches the 4,300 pop-up errors to the 4,800 in-app carts that never reach checkout. It also adds a firmness test that speaks to "too soft for us", and an A/A check.
o2.biggest_mistake: Most tests use orders per session over four weeks with about 10 to 12% detectable lifts, and the schedule stretches to 11 weeks. Test 5 bundles hero image and reviews, so a result cannot be traced to either. There are no per-test money values.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Cheaper add-to-cart reads where they fit, so the plan finishes sooner. Each test needs a rupee value, and the hero image and reviews should be tested separately. The firmness and EMI blanks should be filled with example copy.

reason: Both put the in-app bug first with the right money. Output 1 matches its metrics to the traffic, shows what each test is worth in gross profit, and finishes faster with two lanes. Output 2 reads a little easier and has the firmness test, but its sizing is heavier and slower.
